news_drafts.headline: North Lanarkshire's housing revenue account gap for 2027/28 falls to £4.253m from £7.484m
news_drafts.lead:
North Lanarkshire Council's housing revenue account, the separate ring-fenced account for its own housing stock, paid for by rents, now has a budget gap of £4.253m for 2027/28. The medium-term financial plan presented in August 2026 put the gap at £7.484m. Revised planning assumptions reduced it by £3.231m, according to the paper going to the Housing Committee on 4 November 2026.

The paper sets cost pressures of £7.581m against base budget reductions of £3.328m, which leaves the £4.253m gap. It says the gap is to be reviewed at the December 2026 Council meeting, when estimates and rent levels for 2027/28 are to be approved.

Appendix 2 gives revised gaps for later years. For 2028/29 the gap is £9.751m, against £9.813m in the medium-term plan. For 2029/30 it is £13.998m, against £12.590m. The paper says unbudgeted pressures will be managed where possible through in-year action or unallocated reserves, with recurring impacts addressed in future medium-term financial plans.

news_drafts.headline: Strathclyde concessionary travel scheme shows £844k surplus for 2025/26, after £1.463m deficit a year earlier
news_drafts.lead:
The Strathclyde Concessionary Travel Scheme recorded a surplus of £844k on the provision of services in 2025/26, against a deficit of £1.463m in 2024/25. The figures are in a performance monitoring report on Strathclyde Partnership for Transport (SPT), the regional transport body, in the papers for North Lanarkshire's Environment and Climate Change Committee on 28 October.

Payments to operators fell from £5.451m in 2024/25 to £3.121m in 2025/26. The scheme's cost of services fell over the same period from £5.841m to £3.530m. Income from taxation and non-specific grants rose from £4.095m to £4.178m.

The report's table gives the 2025/26 result in brackets, which the table also uses for surpluses on other lines. It reads: "Deficit on provision of services 1,463 (844)". The figures are in thousands of pounds. The extract does not say why payments to operators were lower in 2025/26.

news_drafts.headline: North Lanarkshire health and social care board plan sets out £67.464m budget gap over three years
news_drafts.lead:
North Lanarkshire's Integration Joint Board (IJB), which oversees health and social care services delegated to it, has a medium-term financial plan (its plan for the next three years, showing the gap between what it expects to spend and what it expects to have). The plan identified a cumulative budget gap of £67.464m over the three years, including £23.923m in 2026/27. The approved budget for 2026/27 is £915.495m, and a recurring savings programme of £22.727m is measured against that year's gap.

The 2026/27 financial monitoring report shows social care services delegated to the partnership projecting an overspend of £4.872m before employee costs. Most of it relates to payments to other bodies, mainly care at home and independent care home places. Budgets were increased by £23.155m for inflation and expected demand, before a £7.900m savings requirement was applied. The paper links the overspend to demand, cost pressures and a shortfall against planned savings.

A separate reserves update, at period 6 (11 September 2026), gives a projected social care overspend of £1.647m. It assumes that sum will be funded from the Risk Reserve, money the board has set aside. It forecasts £5.008m of reserves used for social care. The board's governance progress paper says it approved a savings programme in March 2026 to meet the budget gap and that work on it is "well underway". It gives no savings amount.

findings.committee: Adult Care and Social Work Committee
findings.paper_title: Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report: Adult Social Care Period 6: 1 April to 11 September 2026
findings.headline: Income is forecast to over-recover by £1.165m, including unbudgeted Winter Planning income from NHS Lanarkshire.
findings.detail: The paper says the over-recovery is primarily unbudgeted Winter Planning income and over-recovery on 'Care of Gardens' from the HRA budget. It is partly offset by under-recovery of Integrated Day Services charges, and the Winter Planning expenditure is fully offset by NHS Lanarkshire income.
findings.matters: Reliance on one-off, externally funded income such as Winter Planning money to cover spending is a pattern other councils and their finance teams will recognise when assessing how much of the position is recurring.
findings.quote: The Service anticipates an over recovery of income of £1.165m.

findings.committee: Adult Care and Social Work Committee
findings.paper_title: Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report: Adult Social Care Period 6: 1 April to 11 September 2026
findings.headline: Social Work capital programme is anticipated to break even against a £2.310m approved budget, after a £199,400 trend-based adjustment.
findings.detail: The paper says the 10% trend-based adjustment reflects historic profiling challenges in major capital projects, caused by procurement, contractor and site issues. It says the adjustment gives a more realistic forecast for the Treasury Management Strategy and informs borrowing needs.
findings.matters: The trend-based adjustment shows how a council has reduced its planned capital spend to reflect slippage, which affects its borrowing forecast and treasury planning.
findings.figures: £2.310m approved budget; £199,400 trend-based adjustment; break-even forecast
findings.quote: and is anticipated to outturn with a break-even position.

findings.committee: Adult Care and Social Work Committee
findings.paper_title: Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report: Adult Social Care Period 6: 1 April to 11 September 2026
findings.headline: Any 2026/27 overspend will be fully funded from IJB reserves, with a £1.647m year-end drawdown anticipated.
findings.detail: The paper states that any overspend for the financial year ending 31 March 2027 will be fully funded by IJB reserves. It sets the year-end drawdown equal to the projected overspend, bringing total planned reserve use for 2026/27 to £5.008m.
findings.matters: A council that funds an overspend from reserves rather than in-year savings is showing how its social care pressures are absorbed, which affects how much reserve headroom remains for future years.
findings.figures: £1.647m year-end drawdown; £5.008m total reserves used in 2026/27
findings.quote: will be fully funded by IJB reserves.

findings.committee: Adult Care and Social Work Committee
findings.paper_title: Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report: Adult Social Care Period 6: 1 April to 11 September 2026
findings.headline: £19.048m of Adult Social Care earmarked reserves will be carried forward to 2027/28, including £12.654m for social care demand risk.
findings.detail: The paper says £24.056m of Integration Joint Board reserves are held for specific Adult Social Care commitments, with £5.008m expected to be used in 2026/27. Of the carried-forward balance, £6.394m is set aside for specific projects and £12.654m is earmarked for social care demand risk, including savings shortfalls and unanticipated demand increases.
findings.matters: The size of the demand risk reserve is a direct measure of the cushion available if savings slip or care demand rises, which lenders and peer finance officers will want to compare.
findings.figures: £24.056m total reserves; £5.008m used in 2026/27; £19.048m carried forward; £12.654m social care demand risk
findings.quote: The remaining £19.048m will be carried forward to 2027/28.

findings.committee: Adult Care and Social Work Committee
findings.paper_title: Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report: Adult Social Care Period 6: 1 April to 11 September 2026
findings.headline: Employee costs are forecast to underspend by £3.225m because of slippage in recruitment to posts across the service.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the employee cost underspend to recruitment slippage. It is the main offset to the care cost overspends described elsewhere in the report.
findings.matters: Vacancy-driven underspends are a common way councils offset social care overspends, and whether they persist is a question other finance directors will be asking of their own staffing budgets.
findings.quote: the Service currently anticipates an underspend of £ 3.225m.
